newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Kalimantan riot not subversion - Indonesian police.
newsitem.headline: Kalimantan riot not subversion - Indonesian police.

text.p: Indonesian police have said last week's riot and arson that ended with more than 130 dead in the Kalimantan city of Banjarmasin were not acts of subversion, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.
The local Dinamika Berita daily said the death toll from Friday's riot and shopping centre fire had reached 142, but Antara quoted police in the city on Borneo island as saying 133 died.
Banjarmasin police spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Kusbini Imbar was quoted by Antara as saying that 106 of the 211 people questioned by police over the incident remained in custody.
"There is no indication, however, that the riot was an act of subversion," Imbar said. Government and party officials have suggested the riot was engineered by an unnamed "third party".

Imbar denied the men in detention had come from outside the city or province. "Of the 106 men held, 105 are from Banjarmasin and only one is from the Tabalong district (in the north of the province)," Imbar said.

Dinamika Berita on Monday quoted unnamed officials as saying the remains of at least 136 people had been found in the gutted Mitra Plaza shopping centre after the complex caught fire following arson and looting.

Some shops re-opened in the city on Monday, but several streets remained closed as troops and police remained on guard ahead of Thursday's general election, when Indonesians will choose 425 members of the 500-seat national parliament. The other seats are alloted to the military, which does not vote.
"They are scared to re-open as they think that something might happen again," one resident said.
Dinamika Berita said the bodies found inside the shopping complex were badly charred and appeared to be almost exclusively male.
Officials had said all the shop assistants, most of whom were female, were sent home soon after riots started in the early afternoon when the town's shops were shut.
Another two bodies had been found in both the Lima Cahaya shopping complex and Sarikaya supermarket, while two people died from stab wounds, the newspaper added.

Most of the bodies in Mitra Plaza were found in the Siola department store, many with sharp weapons nearby. Others were located in a Hero Supermarket, Gramedia bookstore, Texas Fried Chicken and Century 21 cinema.

Authorities have said that the victims, who entered the building and set it alight after dark when the city was blacked out, were all looters trapped by the flames after they stayed in the building when riot police and troops began to patrol the streets.

Dinamika Berita quoted unnamed officials as saying they expected the death toll to rise as they had not had an opportunity to search the Hotel Kalimantan and the Jujung Buih shopping complex, both of which were also torched.
The Banjarmasin Post reported on Monday that 164 people had been reported missing to city police.

The riot began on Friday as supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) began to intercept and harass people on their way to a rally of the ruling Golkar party on the final day of Indonesia's violence-plagued election campaign.
Residents said Moslems were angry that Golkar supporters had started noisy parades before Islamic prayers at midday on Friday.
